meta.description: Design prospective power analyses for bulk and pseudobulk RNA-seq, proteomics, and other genomic assays, with realized-FDR gates and explicit clinical-trial handoff.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: Fresh bulk output rejected realized FDR 0.3692738, 0.1849111, 0.1024990, and 0.0598908; no failed candidate is presented as usable.

methodological_ground.detail: The skill distinguishes marginal/per-gene power, gates FDR, uses donors for pseudobulk, and rejects observed power as a null-result explanation.

code_usability.detail: Both shipped R examples completed in retained same-tip runs; the exact pseudobulk rerun recorded exit_code 0 and its post-source sentinel.

functional_suitability.note: Bulk, simulation/FDR, pseudobulk, ATAC/ChIP/methylation, proteomics, budget, observed-power and clinical boundary covered.

reliability.note: Checked wrapper validates inputs; FDR gate rejects non-finite and above-target results.

performance_context.note: Closed-form first, simulation when needed; realistic simulation is intentionally substantive.

agent_usability.note: Decision tree, prompts, version checks and anti-patterns are clear; no machine-readable request contract.

human_usability.note: Natural triggers, scenario routing, examples and escape hatch are discoverable.

security.note: No secrets or arbitrary code execution; inputs are validated before rnapower.

maintainability.note: Clear sections, compatibility guidance, and executable bulk/pseudobulk examples.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger and stop conditions; detailed material remains in one large SKILL.md.

key_strengths: The repaired realized-FDR gate rejects both above-target and non-finite candidates rather than reporting unusable power.
The exact pseudobulk source was rerun to natural exit in an audit-owned process, with both exit code and post-source sentinel retained.
The Skill distinguishes donor-level pseudobulk power from inflated cell-level pseudoreplication and redirects regulated clinical endpoints.

recommendations.title: Pre-specify nonzero Monte Carlo tolerance only when justified
recommendations.problem: The FDR gate permits tolerance but does not define a simulation-error rule for nonzero use.
recommendations.fix: Keep tolerance=0 by default; otherwise pre-specify it, increase nsims, and demonstrate stable accept/reject decisions.
